title: S024 — Randomized SCC / OR-support boundary stress
description: Stress the S023 Phase-B boundary (U subset of C, dU subset of dC, PhaseBOnlyDelta subset of dC) with randomized SCC topologies and correctly constructed OR-group external support.
result_summary: PASS. 100 randomized 5-20-node topologies (seeded, reproducible), biased toward cycles and genuine OR groups. 80 contain a real unfounded SCC (|U|>0); 45 contain a genuine OR group (A AND B) OR G with a separate group label; 500 transitions exercised (forceEvent/negateEvent/severEdge/addEdge). All three invariants hold UNIVERSALLY: U subset of C 500/500; dU subset of dC 500/500; PhaseBOnlyDelta subset of dC 500/500; failures = 0. The S023 OR-group gap is closed. No Phase-B consequence escaped the changed candidate frontier, including cross-SCC cases. Phase B = class B (global algorithm over a local candidate domain). Per the stop condition, Phase-B locality investigation ends; no incremental Phase B, SCC caching, candidate prediction or partial unfounded execution was implemented.
architectural_classification: B - Global algorithm over a local candidate domain. Working architecture: incremental Phase A -> dC -> authoritative global Phase B -> final judgments.
next_architectural_question: Can Phase A itself be implemented incrementally using S021's exact support aggregates while preserving the authoritative derive() semantics?
limitations: 100 topologies / 500 transitions - a finite corpus; empirical, not a proof.
Determinism and branch isolation are by construction but not independently measured.
PhaseBOnlyDelta is defined as judgment changes among unfounded nodes; the strict dU subset of dC assertion is definition-independent and also held.
